dj.name: Mixxx
dj.bestFor: Day-1 learning with zero cost; full features
dj.notes: Recommended first. Concepts transfer to paid apps.

dj.name: Serato DJ Lite
dj.notes: Hardware unlocks more features; Lite is enough to learn decks.

dj.name: rekordbox
dj.notes: Performance mode limits vary by version/hardware.

dj.name: VirtualDJ Home
dj.notes: Licensing differs for paid gigs — check their site.

daw.name: LMMS
daw.bestFor: Pattern-based beat making on a budget

daw.name: Cakewalk by BandLab
daw.notes: Account required; solid for first finished tracks.

daw.name: Tracktion Waveform Free
daw.notes: Paid upgrades exist; Free is enough to learn.

daw.name: Audacity
daw.bestFor: Editing, trimming, simple processing — not a full DAW
daw.notes: Use for cleanup; arrange in a real DAW.

daw.name: Reaper
daw.notes: Fully usable evaluation; buy when ready.

daw.name: FL Studio
daw.bestFor: Pattern/playlist workflow popular with beat makers
daw.notes: Demo can export with limits — check current policy.

daw.name: Ableton Live
daw.bestFor: Clip view, live performance, electronic production
daw.notes: Industry common; Learning Music site is free separately.

daw.name: Logic Pro
daw.bestFor: Mac users wanting a polished all-in-one
daw.notes: One-time purchase via App Store region pricing.

advice: Pick ONE DJ app and ONE DAW for 30 days. Switching weekly kills progress.
Mixxx + LMMS (or Cakewalk on Windows) is a complete free path.
Paid tools are optional upgrades after you finish a mix or track.
